items.title: Metric has no size between lg and xl, and none taken from its box
items.evidence: Metric's value has four sizes: sm --type-small, md --type-prose (the default, src/components/metric/styles.css:70), lg --type-title, xl --type-display-3 (styles.css:104-115; MetricSize at src/components/metric/types.ts:4; data-size at Metric.vue:56). --type-title is a fixed 2.058rem; --type-display-1 is clamp(1.618rem, 1.2rem + 1.6vw, 2.618rem), --type-display-2 clamp(2.058rem, 1.5rem + 2.2vw, 3.33rem), --type-display-3 clamp(2.618rem, 2rem + 3vw, 4.236rem) (src/styles/typography/scale.css:121-123, :134). So display-1 is smaller than title below a viewport of about 858 px, and display-2 equals title below about 406 px. On a phone no existing rung sits between lg and xl (hassio restates the same clamps in px, frontend/src/styles/scale.css:110-113), and every display rung follows the viewport, not the ring. A step between lg and xl that holds on a phone needs a new rung or a size read from a container. No size reads a container today. .metric is display:inline-grid sized by its content (styles.css:25-32), so it cannot be its own size container; a cqi size reads the nearest ancestor container (the cell posture already pads by 2cqi, :140). Metric is unchanged on release/11.1.1 and on bl/dock/wi8. A new size is a new prop value, so a minor. The owner moved the Metric voice change into 11.2.0 (INBOUND O-344; FORMATION-PROGRESS.md:980), so this rides a part 11.2.0 already touches, though O-344 is not on RULINGS-7's dock ready list (:445-462).
items.row: LF-29 (hassio, round 13). The thermostat's reading sits in a ring 120 to 200 px across. lg (--type-title, 32.9 px) looks small in a 144 px ring, and xl (--type-display-3, 41.9 to 67.8 px) crowds the ring's inner edge at its widest clamp. Metric's value has four sizes (metric/styles.css:104-115). The display-1 and display-2 rungs sit between title and display-3 only on a wide screen: below about 858 px display-1 is under title, and below about 406 px display-2 equals it (typography/scale.css:122-123). Every display rung follows the viewport, not the ring, and nothing reads the box the Metric sits in. Placed in 11.2.0 with the Metric voice pass (O-344), as a new size on a part that release already touches. The pass picks a step between lg and xl that holds on a phone, or a size read from a container the consumer marks (cqi), since .metric sizes to its own content and cannot be its own container.
items.reply: 11.2.0 will give Metric a size between lg and xl that still steps up from lg on a phone. The same release's design pass will decide whether a figure can also size itself to a box you mark as its container.

items.title: A face option for Metric's figures
items.dedupe_of: O-344 (with O-218 as its design input)
items.evidence: .metric__value, .metric__unit and .metric__delta all set font-family: var(--font-mono) (src/components/metric/styles.css:69, :80, :98). The value and delta carry tabular-nums lining-nums (:72, :100), and the value is weight 650 (:71). MetricProps has no face prop (src/components/metric/types.ts:32-42). Unchanged on release/11.1.1. INBOUND O-344 (owner, 2026-11-14): 'The Metric voice change moves to 11.2.0 ... the label's capitals, the value's mono face and weight, and the gap before the unit'. O-218 is its design input: value at regular weight, tabular figures kept, shown to the owner before the build.
items.row: LF-33 (hassio, round 13). Every figure on the dashboard is set in the library's mono, so a Metric beside the page's words reads as a second typeface. hassio asks for a face option (for example face="text") that keeps tabular lining figures. The mono face is set on the value, unit and delta (metric/styles.css:69, :80, :98), and no prop changes it. This is the face half of O-344, the owner's move of the Metric voice change into 11.2.0, with O-218 as input. Whether the page's face becomes the default or an option is the owner's choice, shown in that pass. Tabular lining figures stay either way. hassio's ask is recorded beside speedtest's and gaggle's.
items.reply: This is already planned for 11.2.0. Metric's figures will be able to take the page's face, with tabular lining figures kept. That release's design pass settles whether the page's face becomes the default or an option.

items.title: A degree sign that sits on its number; the unit's size on a phone; the value's 3ch floor; a word value
items.dedupe_of: O-344 (the gap before the unit, the value's face and weight); O-84a (the 3ch floor)
items.evidence: .metric__reading lays out the value and unit with gap: 0.3em (src/components/metric/styles.css:59-64). .metric__unit is muted ink at --type-caption (:77-83), which is clamp(0.75rem, 0.71rem + 0.21vw, 1rem) (src/styles/typography/scale.css:99-103), about 12.2 px at 390. .metric__value keeps min-inline-size: 3ch, the mono face, weight 650 and tabular lining figures for any value (:66-75). font-variant-numeric touches digits only, so a word is set apart by the mono face, the weight and the 3ch floor. O-344 (INBOUND:323) books the gap before the unit and the value's face and weight into 11.2.0. O-84a (INBOUND:42) ruled the value content-sized on 2026-09-25 for 10.2.0, and W-0.8 §3.4 wrote it up (docs/tranches/BL/waves/W-0.8.md:129-131) with a migration row (:217). 10.2.0 never shipped (no v10.2.0 tag), W-0.8's part beyond the dock carrier is unplaced (waves/INDEX.md:21), and the floor is still at styles.css:67 on master and on release/11.1.1. Dropping it changes the value's box a consumer may rely on (W-0.8.md:217), so it is a minor and joins O-344. The 14 px floor the ask cites is hassio's design rule (R12-DESIGN M8), not a glass rule; glass states --type-caption's 12 px floor as its caption rung (scale.css:99-103).
items.row: LF-21 (hassio, round 12, with two additions from its closing sweep). (1) A degree sign stands a third of an em off its number, in the unit's smaller, muted type ('21.4 °'; metric/styles.css:63). Signs that set on their number (°, %, ′, ″) should sit tight, by rule or by a prop. (2) The unit is --type-caption (:81), 12.2 px on a 390 phone, under the 14 px floor hassio's design sets for words; the ask notes that a sign drawn at its value's size would answer this too. (3) The value's min-inline-size: 3ch (:67) leaves a hole beside a short number ('0   events'). (4) A word in the value slot ('OK', 'Problem') takes the mono face, weight 650 (:69, :71) and the 3ch floor; tabular figures touch digits only. (1), (2) and (4) fall inside the Metric voice pass the owner moved into 11.2.0 (O-344: the gap before the unit, the value's face and weight); a word kind is one way the pass may answer (4). (3) is O-84a, ruled content-sized in September for 10.2.0, which never shipped; it was never built and is placed again here. Booked as one input to O-344 in 11.2.0.
items.reply: 11.2.0's Metric pass takes all four points. A short value will lose its fixed three-character width, and the pass settles the gap before a sign like ° or %, the unit's size on a phone, and how a word in the value slot is set.

items.title: An avatar status mark that is a glyph, clear of the initials; the sm initial's size
items.evidence: .avatar__status is placed absolutely at inset-inline-end and inset-block-end -0.125rem, with font-size calc(var(--avatar-size) / 2) (src/components/avatar/styles.css:111-125). The slot was drawn for StatusDot's em rungs: an sm dot is 0.5em, a quarter of the face (the slot's notes at :32-39 and :117-120). A mark at 1em is half the face and grows inward from that corner, so it covers the initials. Avatar has no placement prop (AvatarProps at src/components/avatar/Avatar.vue:17-21; the slot at :62-64). The fallback is --type-caption for sm and --type-subheading for md (styles.css:92-105). On a 390 phone sm is 12.2 px in a 40 px face, a ratio of 0.30. md is 20.35 px in 64.7 px, a ratio of 0.31. So scaling md's rule moves sm by under half a pixel; only the 0.4 option changes the look. Avatar is unchanged on release/11.1.1 and on the dock branch.
items.row: LF-22 (hassio, round 12, with an addition from its closing sweep). A resident's face carries a glyph in the status slot (the away arrow, a hand, an alert) at 1em of the slot: 20 px on a 40 px face. The slot sits 0.125rem off the face's corner and was drawn for a StatusDot (avatar/styles.css:111-125), so the glyph covers the lower right of the initial. hassio asks for a rim placement (status-placement="rim") that centres the mark on the face's edge, half outside, keeping the slot's disc and edge. That is a new prop on Avatar: 11.3.0. The sweep's addition: an sm face's initial is --type-caption (styles.css:96), 12.2 px on a phone. That is already about md's proportion. The ask's other option, about 0.4 of the face (16 px), changes the default look, so it goes to the owner with the 11.3.0 Avatar pass.
items.reply: 11.3.0 adds a rim placement for a glyph in the avatar's status slot, so the mark sits half outside the face and clear of the initials. A larger initial on the small avatar would change its default look, so we will ask about it in the same release.

items.title: Windows on a Progress track
items.evidence: Progress fills one span from the track's start to modelValue. --progress-value-percent comes from one fraction (src/components/progress/Progress.vue:41-43, :66-68), and the fill is a translateX by that percent (:174-189). marks are decorative ticks (src/components/progress/types.ts:23-24; Progress.vue:95-108). No prop draws a span that starts after zero, more than one span, an outlined span or a point mark. The root is reka's ProgressRoot, which announces one value as progress (Progress.vue:79-94). The nearest part, Timeline, draws contiguous cumulative spans with a lifecycle fill and interactive end marks (src/components/timeline/types.ts:9, :16-43), with no gaps, no outline and no free point. Unchanged on release/11.1.1.
items.row: LF-23 (hassio, round 12). A plant group's day is one bar, midnight to midnight. Its lit hours are drawn on it as one or two windows: filled while the house will switch them, outlined otherwise, dashed while a change is saving, with a dot at now. Progress fills only from the track's start to one value, and its marks are decorative (progress/Progress.vue:66-68, :182; types.ts:23-24). Timeline's spans are contiguous with interactive ends (timeline/types.ts:16-43). The cards draw their own spans on the public .track-well groove. A span bar on the library's rungs is a new prop or a new part, so it goes to 11.3.0. Its design pass first decides the vehicle: a window of hours is not progress, and a range on Progress would change what a progressbar announces.
items.reply: A bar that draws one or more filled or outlined windows, with a point for now, is a new piece planned for 11.3.0. Until then, drawing your spans on the library's own groove, as you do now, is the right approach.

items.title: A ring meter
items.evidence: src/components has no radial meter (directory listing). The only ring is DotRing, the library's work-in-flight spinner: seven beads, no props, used by Button, InfiniteScroll and EasingPicker, and not exported by design (src/components/_shared/feedback/README.md:16-17, :22, :33-36). Progress is linear only (src/components/progress/Progress.vue:174-197). Unchanged on release/11.1.1.
items.row: LF-24 (hassio, round 12; the brief is the owner's P20 on the dashboard: rounder, more like Apple's rings, slightly thicker). Two rings. A thermostat's 270° sweep shows the set range as a band, with a knob at each end and the working stretch. The Schedule's 24-hour ring shows day and night arcs, two knobs and a now-dot. Where two values share a ring, they are concentric bands. glass-ui has no ring meter, and the dot ring is an internal spinner for work in progress (_shared/feedback/README.md:16-17, :33-36). The ask: a track in the groove register; concentric round-capped arcs over a declared sweep and start angle, in token inks; optional knob seats; a track-width hook; named by the consumer and aware of reduced motion. This is a new part: 11.3.0. It is designed with LF-23, which shows the same day in the same reporting role, and shown to the owner.
items.reply: A ring meter is a new part planned for 11.3.0. It will have concentric round-capped arcs, a sweep and start angle you set, knob seats and a hook for the track's width. Your own rings stay until it ships.

items.title: An Avatar in a dock seat, and two faces in one seat
items.evidence: ddfa8a2ba is only on bl/dock/wi8: git tag --contains finds no tag, and git grep data-dock-glyph finds no hit in src on master, v11.1.0 or release/11.1.1. So on 11.1.0 data-dock-glyph does nothing. The branch's rule sizes a marked box at the seat's glyph size (bl/dock/wi8 src/components/dock/styles/controls/icon-button.css:249-251). RU-87 removes the attribute before 11.2.0 ships (docs/tranches/BL/design/dock/wi8/RULINGS-7.md:319-326, :436, :477) and records Home Assistant's faces as Avatars kept at their own size (:184, :324); the removal is planned, and the attribute is still on the branch tip. The r13 worktree's frontend/src carries no data-dock-glyph (grep finds none): its faces are sized by --avatar-size: 30px (frontend/src/tiles/css/tabs.css:117-119) and stacked in the seat's square on a phone (:133-145), so RU-87's 'no app site' still holds on the tree as read. The seat's glyph size is the --dock-icon-glyph token on both trees (src/components/dock/styles/density.css:241-245; declared at src/styles/tokens/sizing.css:181); daraksha already sizes its seat glyphs from it (RULINGS-7.md:324). The status slot stands 0.125rem past the face's end corner with a 1 px ring (src/components/avatar/styles.css:111-125), so a face given the full glyph size carries its mark that far past it. There is no avatar group in src.
items.row: LF-30 (hassio, round 13, written against ddfa8a2ba). The dock's last seat holds every resident's whole face with its status mark. hassio asks for an Avatar whose status mark stays inside the seat, and for a seat that holds two faces side by side (an avatar group at the seat's glyph size). ddfa8a2ba is on the dock redesign branch only and never shipped, so on 11.1.0 data-dock-glyph does nothing. The redesign removes the attribute before 11.2.0 (RU-87), so 11.2.0 does not size the faces either. The ask says the faces are marked, but the r13 tree's frontend has no such mark, so RU-87's 'no app site' still holds. One face: the status slot stands 0.125rem past the face's corner with a 1 px ring (avatar/styles.css:111-125). The face's size is the site's on 11.1.0 and on 11.2.0, so a face sized that much under the seat's glyph size (--dock-icon-glyph, dock/styles/density.css:241-245) keeps the mark inside the seat. The 30 px line is the site's own size and does not end at 11.2.0. Two faces: an avatar group is a new part, 11.3.0, with LF-22's Avatar pass.
items.reply: data-dock-glyph was never in a release and will not be in 11.2.0, so please drop it. 11.2.0 leaves your faces at the size you give them. The status mark stands 0.125rem past the face's corner with a 1 px ring, so a face that much smaller than --dock-icon-glyph, the seat's glyph size, keeps the mark inside the seat. An avatar group that fits two whole faces, status rings included, in one seat is planned for 11.3.0.

items.title: An open tab seat holds its content at its start
items.evidence: On 11.1.0 the current seat of a run is --dock-open-seat wide, m·P − gap (src/components/dock/styles/run.css:116-126, :539-543). A tab seat is inline-flex with align-items: center and no justify-content (src/components/dock/styles/controls/tab-button.css:12-14), so its glyph and word sit at the seat's start. The run's one selected plate takes the seat's box (run.css:586-596). release/11.1.1 leaves this alone: its tab-button and run diffs are the reduced-motion press and mark only. On the dock redesign branch, 21dcafb37 deletes the rules that widen the current seat, and their vertical pair: 'every seat of a run is one seat wide, the current one included' (bl/dock/wi8 run.css:525-532). The orchestrator's clarification of RU-28 (docs/tranches/BL/design/dock/wi8/RULINGS-4.md:168-170) strikes only the seat grown to three pitches: a control whose content is words keeps its own width in the run, so a worded tab is sized to its content, not clipped to one pitch. RU-28 ships in 11.2.0, with names above the seat as its ship gate (RULINGS-6.md:114). --dock-open-pitches and --dock-open-seat stay declared and unread through 11.2.0 (bl/dock/wi8 run.css:116-117) and are deleted in 12.0.0 (RULINGS-4.md:58-64, :131, :138). Seats are flex: 0 0 auto (bl/dock/wi8 run.css:456-459), so a worded tab is its glyph and word with even padding-inline (tab-button.css:27), and the plate fits it. Centring content in today's open seat would change its look, which a patch does not take.
items.row: LF-14 (hassio, round 12; goes with LF-11 and the owner's P1). A run's open seat is m·P − gap wide by declaration (dock/styles/run.css:539-543). A tab seat lays out its glyph and word at its start, with no justify-content (controls/tab-button.css:12-14). So the selected plate is lopsided round a short word: about 14 px before Schedule's glyph and 24 after its word at three pitches, and about 70 px empty at four. The library's own demo dock does the same. Cured on the 11.2.0 line: the dock redesign deletes the widened current seat (21dcafb37, ruling RU-28). Every seat, the current one included, is as wide as its content; a worded tab keeps its words (RU-28's clarification), so the plate is even round the word. --dock-open-pitches is unread from 11.2.0, so hassio's four pitches stop doing anything, and the Home Assistant draft message should say so. No 11.1.2 cure: centring would change the seat's look, and the seat it would centre in is deleted one minor later.
items.reply: 11.2.0 removes the widened current seat. A selected tab will be exactly as wide as its glyph and word, with even padding, and the plate will sit evenly round it. The four-pitch setting will have no effect from then on and can go.

items.title: Round 13 amendments: LF-1 reaches --spacing, LF-2 gains a 44 px floor on a selectable Chip, LF-26 withdrawn
items.evidence: LF-1: Chip's sizes are Tailwind utilities (src/components/chip/chipVariants.ts:7-23); an icon Chip is size-10 at md and size-12 at lg. Glass emits them as calc(var(--spacing,0.25rem) * n) into dist/styles/components.css through emitComponentUtilities (src/styles/index.css:299-307). src declares no --spacing (git grep finds none), so the rem fallback or the consumer's Tailwind theme sets it. After O-377a, LF-1 itself moved from 11.2.0 to 12.0.0 (docs/tranches/BL/design/dock/wi8/RULINGS-6.md:195, :202: 'it touches every row of density.css, which 12.0.0 collapses'; RULINGS-7.md:562). LF-2: a selectable or action Chip is interactive (src/components/chip/Chip.vue:62). Under a coarse pointer an interactive Chip already takes min-inline-size and min-block-size var(--touch-target, 2.75rem) (src/styles/glass/glass-chip.css:97-101), the same in v11.1.0. The dashboard restates --touch-target: 44px on :host (hassio frontend/src/styles/scale.css:63), so a selectable Chip on a coarse pointer should compute 44 px. The 42 px reading fits a static icon Chip at lg (size-12 at a 14 px root), or a fine pointer. LF-26: --slider-touch-target: 1.5rem is deliberate (src/styles/tokens/sizing.css:298-305) and can only raise the target (src/components/slider/styles.css:124-133). O-377a covered LF-1 to LF-13, so LF-26 was never booked.
items.row: hassio's three amendments, round 13 (AMENDS.md). (1) LF-1 now also covers Tailwind's --spacing. Chip's sizes are spacing utilities (chip/chipVariants.ts:7-23), emitted as calc(var(--spacing, 0.25rem) × n), and glass declares no --spacing. So inside Home Assistant's 14 px root an icon Chip is 35 px at md and 42 px at lg. Placed with LF-1, which moved after O-377a from 11.2.0 to 12.0.0, where the size tokens are collapsed (dock rulings 6, the base size). The base size there must reach every utility-sized part, not only the tokens. (2) LF-2 now also asks for a 44 px floor on a selectable Chip under a coarse pointer. That floor already ships in 11.1.0: an interactive Chip, selectable or action, takes --touch-target (2.75rem) as its minimum under a coarse pointer (glass/glass-chip.css:97-101). hassio restates --touch-target at 44 px, so the 42 px reading needs its Chip's mode and pointer; a static Chip has no floor (chip/Chip.vue:62). LF-2's capsule half stays in 11.1.2, as O-377a placed it. (3) LF-26 (the slider's coarse target at 44 px) is withdrawn. The 24 px target is deliberate (tokens/sizing.css:298-305), and the dashboard raises it through --slider-touch-target. Nothing was booked for it.
items.reply: LF-1 now covers --spacing too and moves with it to 12.0.0, where one base size will reach every utility-sized part. A selectable or action Chip already floors at --touch-target on a coarse pointer in 11.1.0; if yours reads 42 px, please send its mode and the pointer you measured with. LF-26 is recorded as withdrawn.

changed: LF-29: the claim that existing rungs sit between lg and xl, so no new token is needed, does not hold on a phone. --type-display-1 is under --type-title below a viewport of about 858 px, and --type-display-2 equals it below about 406 px (scale.css:122-123; hassio restates the same clamps at frontend/src/styles/scale.css:110-113). Every display rung follows the viewport, not the ring. Evidence, row and reply corrected, and the reply no longer promises a size taken from existing rungs. Release kept (O-344 has the owner's 11.2.0 word, though it is not on RULINGS-7's dock ready list).

LF-21: verdict and release kept. Four corrections: the 14 px floor is hassio's design rule, not glass's; font-variant-numeric touches digits only, so a word value is set apart by the mono face, weight 650 and the 3ch floor; O-84a's booking release (10.2.0) never shipped and its wave part is unplaced (waves/INDEX.md:21); the reply promised how a word will be set, which O-344's pass has not yet decided.

LF-30: the row said hassio now marks its faces with data-dock-glyph, but the r13 worktree's frontend/src has none (faces sized at tiles/css/tabs.css:117-119 and :133-145), so RU-87's 'no app site' still holds. The reply now answers the one-face half: the status slot's 0.125rem and 1 px overhang (avatar/styles.css:111-125) against --dock-icon-glyph.

LF-14: verdict kept. Evidence strengthened with RU-28's clarification (RULINGS-4.md:168-170): a worded control keeps its own width, so the branch comment 'one seat wide' does not clip a worded tab. Added RU-28's ship gate (RULINGS-6.md:114) and the release-rule reason for no patch (centring is a look change).
